description: Forge step F2: an edited level loads and plays. One ordinary client launch opens the placements of the extracted base Complex arena (226 pads, 19 player starts, 35 objects), adds a player start 40 units in front of the first one and a copy of the first weapon pickup 60 units in front of it, leaves the first ammo crate out (all four difficulty exclusion bits, the way base levels thin a level for one difficulty), and saves the result as the mod level 'Forge_Edit' through --debug-forge-level (the open and save calls the Forge editor makes; the save is the mod author's, the one the other in-game creators use). The same launch then starts an offline Combat Simulator match on mod:arena_forge_edit with three simulants and waits for the player to spawn and walk. The proof that the game read the edited files and not the template's: its navigation record counts 228 pads and 228 volumes, its level graph has 228 trigger volume nodes for 228 bounds rows (the game refuses a level where those two differ, so each pad Forge adds brings its node), and its setup compiles to 36 records and 20 spawns. What this does not prove: that the copied pickup is drawn where it was put, that the crate left out is gone, or that a player or simulant used the new start; nothing here looks at the world. No mod exists before the launch. A level made from a base arena holds data from the player's own game files and is local only.

input_sequence.comment: Pause the script until the ordinary Combat Simulator player is continuously spawned, live, controllable and walking on the edited level. The level was made by the first CLI fast paths, before the room launch flags.
Six seconds on the level, then a scripted exit.
